title: Microsoft 365 Certified: Collaboration Communications Systems Engineer Associate (MS-721)

nodes.title: Microsoft 365 licensing: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Microsoft 365 is sold in subscription plans that bundle productivity apps, security, and device management. MS-900 exams test which plan includes which features and the volume licensing options.

flashcards.front: Microsoft 365 Business vs Enterprise plans — key split?
flashcards.back: Business plans (Basic/Standard/Premium) are capped at 300 users. Enterprise plans (E1/E3/E5) have no user cap and include advanced compliance and security features.

flashcards.front: What does Microsoft 365 E5 add over E3?
flashcards.back: E5 adds advanced security (Defender for Identity, Defender for Cloud Apps), advanced compliance (Purview), and Power BI Pro — roughly doubles the cost of E3.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Volume Licensing vs Microsoft 365 subscription?
flashcards.back: Volume Licensing (EA, CSP) offers negotiated pricing, centralised management, and payment flexibility for large organisations; subscriptions are per-user/month via direct or partner channels.
Office 365 is the older brand for productivity apps + cloud services. Microsoft 365 adds Windows 10/11 Enterprise licences and advanced security/compliance tools.

questions.q: Contoso is enabling Microsoft Teams Phone with Direct Routing for 500 users. The team already owns a Session Border Controller (SBC) that is certified for Teams. Which prerequisite record must exist in public DNS before the SBC can pair with the Teams tenant?
choices: An A record for the SBC's fully qualified domain name (FQDN) resolvable from the public internet
A TXT record containing the tenant ID at the root of the SIP domain
A SRV record advertising _sip._tcp for the SBC's local network
A CNAME pointing sip.contoso.com to sipdir.online.lync.com
questions.explanation: Direct Routing requires the SBC to be reachable from Microsoft's Teams infrastructure over the public internet on TCP 5061 (SIP over TLS). Microsoft will only accept a signaling connection if the SBC FQDN resolves via a public A record and the certificate on that FQDN matches. Tenant ownership of the SIP domain is proven when the domain is added to Microsoft 365, not through a TXT record on the SBC. SRV records are used by some on-premises SIP clients but are not part of the SBC pairing flow. The CNAME to sipdir.online.lync.com belongs to hybrid Skype for Business deployments, not Teams Direct Routing.

questions.q: A Teams administrator needs to assign a phone number from Microsoft's inventory to a user in the United States and enable outbound calling to any country. The tenant has Teams Phone Standard licenses. Which additional license or plan must be assigned to the user?
choices: Communications Credits only, without any calling plan
Microsoft Teams Rooms Pro
Teams Phone with Calling Plan (Domestic and International) or Pay-As-You-Go Calling Plan
Microsoft 365 Business Voice, which includes international dialing by default
questions.explanation: To receive a Microsoft-provided phone number and place international calls, the user needs an actual calling plan on top of Teams Phone Standard — either the Domestic and International Calling Plan (bundled minutes) or the Pay-As-You-Go Calling Plan (per-minute). Communications Credits alone cover overages and toll-free minutes but do not entitle the user to a Microsoft phone number. Teams Rooms Pro is a device license, not a user calling entitlement. Microsoft 365 Business Voice was retired and its domestic-only bundle never covered international dialing without add-ons.

questions.q: You must ensure that when users at the Seattle office dial 911, dispatchers receive the specific building and floor as the emergency location. Which Teams Phone feature enforces this by mapping network endpoints to civic addresses?
choices: Location-Based Routing (LBR) with PSTN Usage records
Dynamic Emergency Calling with a Location Information Service (LIS) that maps subnets, WAPs, switches, or ports to emergency addresses
Call Park policy scoped to the Seattle site
Caller ID policy overriding the outbound number with the site DID
questions.explanation: Dynamic Emergency Calling relies on a Location Information Service that associates network identifiers (subnet, chassis/port, BSSID, or LLDP switch data) with a validated civic address. When a Teams client dials an emergency number, it reports the discovered location to PSTN so responders arrive at the exact building and floor. Location-Based Routing prevents toll bypass by restricting where calls can route based on user location, but it does not communicate an emergency address. Call Park and Caller ID policies are unrelated to 911 dispatch.

questions.q: The Contoso helpdesk needs a single number that rings a group of agents in parallel, waits up to 45 seconds, then rolls to voicemail. Callers should not hear a hold queue or greeting — the flow must ring the agents directly. Which Teams Phone construct fits?
choices: A Call Queue with the Attendant routing method configured to serial ring
A Call Queue with an agent group and no music-on-hold, using Attendant call routing set to All-at-once (parallel)
An Auto Attendant with a menu that dial-transfers to each helpdesk agent in turn
A Shared Line Appearance policy configured for delegated ringing
questions.explanation: Call Queues support parallel (All-at-once/Attendant) ringing where every available agent receives the call simultaneously, with a configurable timeout before the overflow action (voicemail here). Serial routing rings agents one-by-one, which does not match the requirement. Auto Attendants play menus and route calls but do not fan-out to a group of agents in parallel. Shared Line Appearance lets a delegate answer a manager's line — it is not a helpdesk queue.

questions.q: Users complain that outbound calls from Teams frequently drop after two minutes when routed through the on-premises SBC. TLS handshake succeeds and initial audio is present. On the SBC you see BYE messages from Teams every ~2 minutes. Which cause is most consistent with the symptom?
choices: The SBC certificate expired and needs renewal
A firewall or NAT device on the media path is aging out UDP flows because RTP/SRTP is not being kept alive end-to-end (media path issue)
The tenant is missing the Microsoft Calling Plan license
The user is signed in from an unmanaged BYOD device
questions.explanation: Signaling that works (TLS/SIP over 5061) with media that fails after a couple of minutes is the classic fingerprint of a UDP path problem — most often a firewall or NAT device whose session table ages out inactive UDP entries. Teams issues a BYE when the media stream stops. An expired certificate would break signaling from the start. Calling-plan licensing has no effect once the call is up. Device management state does not affect mid-call media transport.

questions.q: You need to prevent Teams users in the London office from placing PSTN calls that would leave the UK via a US-based SBC (toll bypass), while still allowing them to place local UK calls. Which Teams Phone feature enforces this?
choices: Location-Based Routing (LBR) with network sites and PSTN Usage records that restrict cross-region routing
Emergency Calling policy with a US emergency number
Tenant Dial Plan that rewrites all numbers to +1 format
Caller ID policy set to Anonymous for London users
questions.explanation: Location-Based Routing is the mechanism that prevents toll bypass. You define network sites tied to trusted IP subnets, then tag PSTN Usage records so calls from the London site can only egress via UK-approved voice routes and SBCs. Emergency Calling policy handles 911/999 dispatch, not toll compliance. A Tenant Dial Plan normalizes dialed digits but does not restrict which SBC handles the call. Caller ID policy controls what the called party sees — it does not stop the call from egressing through the wrong country.

questions.q: You are creating a new Auto Attendant that must answer the main number, greet in English, offer a menu ("Press 1 for Sales, 2 for Support"), and after hours route callers to a shared voicemail. Which pair of objects must exist before you can save the Auto Attendant?
choices: A dedicated Teams Rooms Pro license and a Common Area Phone
A resource account with a phone number assigned to the Auto Attendant, plus at least one call target (user, Call Queue, or shared voicemail) referenced by the menu options
A Direct Routing SBC even if the tenant uses Microsoft Calling Plans
A Tenant Dial Plan matching the country of the main number
questions.explanation: An Auto Attendant is reached through a resource account (Virtual User license + phone number) — that is what actually receives the inbound call — and every menu option must resolve to a callable destination (user, Call Queue, external number, or shared voicemail). Without both, the AA has no way to answer or route. Teams Rooms Pro and Common Area Phone licenses are for devices, not voice apps. A Direct Routing SBC is only required if you are not using Microsoft Calling Plans/Operator Connect. A Tenant Dial Plan is optional and controls user dialing behavior, not AA creation.

nodes.title: Mixed exam topics: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Some exam objectives don't fit neatly into a single domain — they span protocols, tools, or concepts covered briefly in multiple sections. These cards treat each item as a stand-alone fact, the way an exam question presents it: one concept, one answer.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a hub, a switch, and a router?
flashcards.back: Hub: Layer 1, repeats every frame to all ports — all devices share bandwidth, collisions guaranteed. Switch: Layer 2, forwards frames using a MAC address table to only the destination port — full duplex, no collisions, each port gets full bandwidth. Router: Layer 3, makes forwarding decisions based on IP address, connects different networks. Hub is legacy; switches dominate LAN; routers are at network edges.

flashcards.front: What is RAID 5 and how many drives can it tolerate losing?
flashcards.back: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across at least 3 drives. Any single drive failure can be recovered by reconstructing missing data from the remaining drives and parity. It cannot tolerate 2 simultaneous drive failures. Effective capacity = (N-1) × drive size. Read performance is excellent; write requires parity recalculation. RAID 6 tolerates 2 failures using double parity.

flashcards.front: What does a proxy server do, and how does a forward proxy differ from a reverse proxy?
flashcards.back: Forward proxy: sits between clients and the internet on behalf of clients — used for content filtering, caching, and anonymizing outbound requests (the server sees the proxy's IP). Reverse proxy: sits in front of servers on behalf of the server — used for load balancing, SSL termination, caching, and hiding backend topology (the client sees the proxy's IP). Both intermediate HTTP, but they protect opposite sides.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of a DMZ in network architecture?
flashcards.back: A demilitarized zone is a network segment between the untrusted internet and the trusted internal network, typically protected by two firewalls (or two interfaces on one firewall). Public-facing services (web, email, DNS) sit in the DMZ: internet can reach them but not the internal network; if the DMZ host is compromised, the inner firewall still blocks access to the internal LAN.

questions.q: The compliance team requires that all Teams meetings hosted by the finance department be recorded automatically and that recordings are retained for seven years. Which combination best meets both requirements?
choices: A Teams Meeting policy scoped to the finance group with "Record automatically" enabled, plus a Purview retention policy or label applied to OneDrive/SharePoint that retains recordings for seven years
A Teams Meeting policy that disables recording so users cannot delete evidence, combined with a legal hold on the mailbox
A Teams Live Events policy scoped to the finance group with attendee reporting turned on
A Microsoft Purview eDiscovery Premium case created before each meeting
questions.explanation: Auto-recording is a Teams Meeting policy setting ("Record automatically") applied to the organizer — scoping the policy to a finance group covers the automation half. Recordings land in the organizer's OneDrive (or the channel's SharePoint site for channel meetings), so retention is enforced with a Purview retention policy or label targeting those locations. Disabling recording obviously does not create recordings. Live Events is a different meeting type used for large broadcasts, not standard finance meetings. Creating an eDiscovery case per meeting is neither scalable nor how retention is enforced.

questions.q: During a Teams meeting an internal user complains of one-way audio: they can hear the remote party but the remote party cannot hear them. The user is at home, using a headset, and other meetings work fine on their laptop's built-in mic. Which first diagnostic step is most likely to reveal the cause?
choices: Restart the SBC in the datacenter because Direct Routing is likely at fault
Check the Teams client Device settings to confirm the correct microphone is selected and verify Windows privacy settings allow microphone access for Teams
Open a Microsoft support ticket to reassign the Teams Phone Standard license
Force the user to sign in from an Azure Virtual Desktop session
questions.explanation: One-way audio limited to a specific user and a specific device points to local mic capture — the wrong input device is selected in the client, or Windows privacy has revoked mic access for Teams. Checking Device settings and OS privacy is the fastest, safest first step. The SBC handles PSTN calls, not internal Teams meetings, so restarting it is irrelevant and disruptive. License state does not affect microphone capture. Moving the user to AVD is a workaround that skips the root cause and adds unrelated variables.

questions.q: The marketing team wants to broadcast an all-hands to 8,000 employees with a produced-video feel: a small production crew controls what attendees see, attendees watch in view-only mode, and the recording is available afterwards. Which Teams product should you plan?
choices: A standard Teams Meeting with the large-gallery view enabled
A Teams Webinar with the RSVP registration form
A Teams Town Hall (formerly Live Events) with a production team, view-only attendee experience, and on-demand replay
A Teams Call Queue configured with music-on-hold for 8,000 callers
questions.explanation: Teams Town Hall is the successor to Live Events and is designed exactly for one-to-many broadcasts up to tens of thousands of attendees, with a production/presenter group, a view-only attendee experience, moderated Q&A, and on-demand playback. Standard meetings and Webinars are two-way and cap out below Town Hall's scale for a produced broadcast experience. A Call Queue is a PSTN routing construct and has nothing to do with company-wide video broadcast.

questions.q: A Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows console shows a red banner reading "Your account couldn't be signed in — device is not compliant". The device has a Teams Rooms Pro license, is Azure AD joined, and Intune enrollment is present. Which Conditional Access exclusion is required to keep MTR devices signed in?
choices: Exclude the Teams Rooms resource account from all Conditional Access policies
Exclude the Teams Rooms resource account from Conditional Access policies that require MFA or device compliance, or use policies that target only users (not resource accounts)
Assign the Teams Rooms resource account the Global Administrator role
Add the Teams Rooms IP address to the tenant's Trusted Locations list
questions.explanation: Teams Rooms resource accounts sign in unattended and cannot satisfy interactive MFA prompts. Microsoft's guidance is to exclude MTR resource accounts from Conditional Access policies that enforce MFA or device compliance, or scope those policies so they do not target the resource accounts. Excluding them from all CA policies is broader than needed and weakens security posture. Making the account a Global Administrator is neither required nor appropriate. A Trusted Location can reduce prompts but does not resolve the compliance grant when the CA policy requires a compliant device.

questions.q: An organization wants to onboard 30 new Teams Rooms on Android devices at scale. Which Microsoft-supported service registers each device, assigns a resource account, and applies configuration without the deployment team touching each console physically?
choices: Microsoft Teams Rooms Pro Management portal with device provisioning tags and remote sign-in via verification code
Manually pairing each device to a laptop over USB and running a PowerShell script
Windows Autopilot self-deploying mode with an Intune Autopilot profile
Direct Routing SBC-based provisioning of each device MAC address
questions.explanation: Teams Rooms Pro Management (the portal at portal.rooms.microsoft.com) provisions Android MTR consoles remotely: the device displays a verification code that an administrator claims in the portal to bind it to a resource account and configuration profile. Autopilot is for Windows PCs and cannot provision Android MTR consoles. USB tethering and per-device scripts do not scale to 30 rooms. Direct Routing SBCs handle PSTN signaling, not device provisioning.
